why_this_file_exists: Phase 4 S7 declares seven authority moves and lands four: Hypershot, Abyssal Unmake, Bloodsong, Shadowflame. Three of the four landed. Shadowflame did not, and the reason was not effort or judgement but a declaration shape the campaign had not ruled: its walk half delivers its number as a rider on an existing damage event rather than as a packet, and no MechanicCapability shape could say that. The second entry is a plan/tree divergence a landed slice took deliberately and could not resolve from an implementation lane. Written down as a dated, gated artifact rather than as commit-body prose, because prose is what the next baseline re-capture absorbs.
how_an_entry_closes: An entry moves from defects[] to retired[] only when its contradiction is resolved by a ruling recorded in the umbrella, and only together with the gate test's own inversion: the reproducer stops reproducing and the test asserts the resolved property instead. Deleting an entry is not closing it, and a retired entry keeps its original what/why so the reader can see what was ruled and against what.

defects.raised_by: the S7 implementation lane, in the commit that landed the move
defects.what: The umbrella's semantic-authority table rules bloodsong.expose_weakness COUPLED_AUTHORITATIVE. The slice landed COUPLED_AUTHORITATIVE_WITH_PAIR_PREVIEW.
defects.why: Plain COUPLED_AUTHORITATIVE is unconstructible for this mechanic. item_support_effects._check_cross_participant_authority resolves a damage_modifier packet's authority through trigger_stream.CROSS_PARTICIPANT_AUTHORITIES, whose three members are the ones that say a second engine can see the mechanic. Bloodsong's pair pricer (damage._add_expose_weakness) still exists — golden pins it and deleting it is a pair-engine change this slice does not make — so a second engine does see it, and declaring otherwise makes the packet fail to build at runtime.
defects.why_the_ruling_is_still_honoured: The row's binding obligation is 'pair and walk are not numerically equivalent; never unify inside a slice labelled a pure refactor'. Nothing was unified: one side is named the answer, the other is tagged THEORETICAL and excluded from every roster total, and the slice is labelled semantic.
defects.for_the_umbrella_owner: Either the table's member is refreshed to the constructible one, or the pair pricer is scheduled for deletion in a slice that owns damage.py and can move the pair golden. An implementation lane may not choose.
defects.reproducer: Set the walk half's authority to Authority.COUPLED_AUTHORITATIVE and run pytest tests/test_item_support_effects.py: every Bloodsong packet raises ValueError('Bloodsong — Expose Weakness modifies another participant's damage but names no Authority').

retired.raised_by: the S7 implementation lane, before its first Shadowflame src/ edit
retired.what: shadowflame.cinderbloom's authority move cannot be declared. The mechanic's coupled half is an AmpBonus rider on its triggering Damage event (phase-4 ruling: 'a LivePredicate, never a window; the bonus becomes a rider on its triggering event, read before absorption'), so it authors no packet. The registry has no shape for that: a PAIRED walk half must carry a packet_source (trigger_stream._validate_pairing, 'the walk half's packet is what the pair half is paired against'), and a WALK row carrying a packet_source with a cross-participant authority joins scripts/golden_snapshot.cross_participant_producers() — the set D-07 rules is exactly the six damage_modifier producers and umbrella criterion 3 pins at six. Cinderbloom's declared Subject is HOLDER: it amplifies the holder's own magic and true damage on a predicate about the target's live health, so it modifies no other participant's damage and declaring it a seventh cross-participant producer would make a ruled count wrong.
retired.why_this_lane_may_not_fix_it: Both candidate fixes are somebody else's. (a) Generalising Pairing/packet_source so a PAIRED half may declare a rider source is a Phase 2 structural rule, and the runbook's ownership map gives this lane only view_tags, holder_stacking and the HolderStacking enum in trigger_stream.py. (b) Adding a rider-delivery field to MechanicCapability is forbidden outright: phase 4 writes exactly two fields there 'and no third'. Choosing between them is a design ruling, and an implementation lane inventing one is how a declaration stops meaning what the umbrella says it means.
retired.resolved_by: Amendment C to D-07, ruled by the orchestrator and recorded in docs/plans/2026-08-08-silent-failure-campaign.md beside D-07 and the semantic-authority table.
retired.resolution: The structure was amended, which is the half the escalation asked for. A PAIRED walk half may now be RIDER-DELIVERED: its delivery reference is the rider stamp (trigger_stream.RiderDelivery) rather than a packet source, carried inside the existing packet_source field, so Phase 4's exactly-two-fields rule on MechanicCapability stands and no third field was added. The cross-participant producer derivation moved onto D-07's own semantic — every packet modifying ANOTHER participant's damage, trigger_stream.cross_participant_packet_source — so a rider-delivered half, which amplifies its own holder's event, is not a member; the ruled count of six and umbrella criterion 3 are untouched, and tests/test_trigger_stream.py pins the six by name.
retired.what_this_retirement_does_not_close: The Shadowflame authority move itself is unblocked, not landed. Whoever lands it still owes the bench-population enumeration before its first src/ edit (R-20's second half): the coupled-golden population measured 0 for a stated reason, but the bench population is not zero and was deliberately not enumerated — the three enemy-bearing bench scenarios may propose Shadowflame as a candidate, and a walk-side Cinderbloom could move a candidate's score there.
what_is_already_true_and_needs_no_ruling: The pair half already declares authority=COUPLED_AUTHORITATIVE_WITH_PAIR_PREVIEW, which is the correct ruling and was landed in Phase 2.

The preview-exclusion mechanism the move needs already exists and is live: damage.py stamps a row with pair_preview_of, trigger_stream declares the pair lane THEORETICAL, and participant_timeline._pair_packet keeps previewed rows and their events out of everything the roster composes. Shadowflame's move needs exactly two lines of it — a view_tag=ViewTag.THEORETICAL on the pair row and a pair_preview_of stamp on damage._add_shadowflame_cinderbloom's breakdown row — plus the walk half, which now has a shape.

The kernel-side work is scoped and unblocked: a LiveAmp value field on SurvivalAction, evaluated by tag inside survival/transitions._apply_live_packet_chain, which is already the pre-absorption point the ruling requires.
retired.population_measured_before_the_lane_stop: The coupled-golden population for this move is genuinely 0, and now for a stated reason rather than an assumed one: six committed coupled scenarios equip Shadowflame (the Syndra pins) and in all six the coupled composition holds no enemy participant at all — combat.participants is main plus ally:Syndra and both breakdown rows total 0.0 — so no subject exists whose live health could satisfy the predicate. The other seven scenarios equip no Shadowflame. The pair snapshot is untouched by a walk-side rider. The bench population is NOT zero and was not enumerated: the three enemy-bearing bench scenarios may propose Shadowflame as a candidate, and a walk-side Cinderbloom could move a candidate's score there. Whoever lands this move owes that enumeration before its first src/ edit (R-20's second half).
retired.reproducer: Add a WALK MechanicCapability for shadowflame.cinderbloom with pairing=PAIRED and packet_source=None: trigger_stream raises TriggerRegistryError at import ('is PAIRED and declares no packet_source'). Give it any packet_source instead and tests/test_trigger_stream.py's producer-identity assertion goes red, because cross_participant_producers() gains a seventh member.
retired.reproducer_after_retirement: Inverted, and asserted by the gate: a PAIRED walk half carrying RiderDelivery('Shadowflame — Cinderbloom') validates, cross_participant_packet_source returns None for it, and the producer set is still the ruled six. A PAIRED half carrying neither a packet source nor a rider stamp still fails validation, which is the half of the old shape that had to survive the amendment.
